description:
Focus Music | Sarod Instrumental for Deep Work & Mental Clarity | 1.5 Hours

For mornings when your mind feels foggy and you need to actually focus — this is your reset.

90 minutes of slow, meditative Sarod (deeper cousin of the sitar, with a rich resonant character) designed to quiet mental noise and settle you into focused work.

What you'll hear:
• Slow Hindustani Sarod — contemplative phrasing, no sudden shifts
• Soft tabla and tanpura grounding the sound
• Recorded warm and acoustic, no electronic processing
• Long sustained phrases with space between — nothing distracting

Best for:
• Deep work sessions
• Reading, writing, coding
• Mental clarity after screen fatigue
• Meditation before a task-heavy morning
• ADHD-friendly ambient focus

Press play. Close the tabs. Get into it.
suno_prompt_note: PARKED — user's separate Suno exploration. CALM rule mandatory. Sarod-specific: emphasize warm resonant plucked-string character ('deep warm sarod with sustained resonance, meend slides, sympathetic strings'). Sarod is fretless plucked — more contemplative than sitar's crisp attack. Pacing reference: Mental Clarity Music Slow Sarod Brain Fog Reset (May 15) achieved 37% AVD — match that character. Suggested opener: 'No vocals. Solo sarod, Raga Bhimpalasi, deep contemplative focus mood. Cold open mid-melody. 55 BPM, sustained melodic phrases with meend ornaments. Tanpura drone, sparse soft tabla — sarod leads always. Same 3 instruments, seamless loop. No vocals, no humming.'

experiment.type: title A/B — VidIQ vs empirical retention head-to-head
experiment.hypothesis: Head-to-head test between two defensible leads: (A) Mental Clarity Music (VidIQ 65) replicating the 37% AVD May 15 Sarod formula, vs (B) Focus Music (VidIQ 84) — highest cognitive VidIQ but Focus Music has spotty history on Santoor/Sitar attempts. Same everything else. Isolates VidIQ signal vs catalog performance as competing rules.
experiment.success_criteria: One variant wins by >5pp AND overall ship hits AVD>=25%, views>=8K in 7 days
experiment.failure_criteria: Both variants underperform (AVD<18% AND views<3K each) = Sarod cognitive lane is saturated regardless of framing
experiment.neutral_zone: AVD 18-25% or views 3-8K = directional, needs second attempt with different framing
experiment.what_we_learn: If A wins → replicate proven-formula leads, deprioritize VidIQ. If B wins → trust VidIQ over catalog history. If tied → both signals valid, decide case-by-case.
